catalogRecord.scanSource: Photogrammetric capture by Ørjan Sandland (orjansandland) records the granite column and its pedestal at Vigeland Park. The model isolates the monument from the surrounding terrace and separate figure groups. The pedestal’s floor-contact underside is open and unrecorded. Atrium simplified the geometry for web delivery while retaining the recorded appearance. Small surface details are softer and the pedestal appears more faceted in this web version.
catalogRecord.note: Intertwined human figures climb and support one another in a densely carved granite column. Vigeland modelled the work in 1924–1925; the stone was carved at the park from 1929 to 1942. The museum’s park chronology credits Ivar Broe, Nils Jønsson and Karl Kjær as the stone carvers. This capture includes the column and its pedestal, while the surrounding plateau and its separate granite groups are outside its scope. The complete captured column-and-pedestal dimensions are unconfirmed; published column measurements are not treated as a physical calibration of this assembly.

caption.text: Intertwined bodies cover the column, with heads, backs and limbs emerging at different depths. Move around it to follow one figure into the next. Vigeland modeled the composition in 1924–1925; Ivar Broe, Nils Jønsson and Karl Kjær carved the granite from 1929 to 1942. This model records the column and its pedestal.

Two crouching figures rest back to back and clasp their raised hands. Their bent legs spread the weight while the linked arms make another connection overhead. Turn the group to compare the faces and the spaces enclosed by their limbs. The provider identifies the granite sculpture as Vigeland’s Two Girls Back to Back; its exact date and site remain unconfirmed.
